title: AI exposure estimates can change when the measuring model changes
source_unit: large-language-model ratings of occupational AI exposure and downstream statistical estimates
geography: United States occupational and county-level analyses

denominator.unit: frontier language models applying the same occupational-exposure rubric

mean_exposure_divergence.unit: divergence across models in mean occupational AI-exposure estimates

observations.method: The study applies the same exposure-rating rubric to identical occupational tasks using three frontier language models and compares the resulting exposure measures.
observations.uncertainty: The result concerns one family of LLM-based measurement procedures and does not show that every AI-exposure measure is equally unstable. Agreement depends on the rubric, prompts, task descriptions, models, and aggregation choices.
observations.subgroup: Occupational task ratings produced by different model annotators; the unit is a measurement procedure, not a worker's self-reported exposure.
observations.counterinterpretation: Model disagreement could reflect genuine ambiguity in task descriptions or differences in model knowledge rather than a failure of all exposure concepts; non-LLM task measures may behave differently.

denominator.unit: individual- and county-level statistical specifications using the replicated exposure measures

individual_coefficient_variation.unit: variation in downstream individual-level coefficient magnitudes across model annotators

county_result_direction.unit: change in county-level difference-in-differences result depending on annotator

observations.method: The authors rerun downstream difference-in-differences exercises after substituting exposure measures generated by different model annotators.
observations.uncertainty: These are sensitivity exercises around model-generated exposure measures, not a new causal estimate of AI's labor-market effect. The abstract does not establish which annotator or specification is correct.
observations.subgroup: Individual-level and county-level downstream analyses; the estimated direction and magnitude vary with the exposure measurement source.
observations.counterinterpretation: A changed coefficient can indicate measurement error, model disagreement, specification sensitivity, or genuine uncertainty in the underlying construct; it should not be read as proof that the substantive effect is zero or reversed.

related_sources.claim: NBER DOI record for the multi-model replication study.

boundary: This finding is a measurement-quality counterexample for the AI-work lane. It shows that some LLM-generated exposure inputs are not stable across models and that downstream estimates can change with the input. It does not invalidate every AI-exposure measure, estimate actual worker displacement, or replace substantive labor-market evidence.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: NBER working-paper URL response retrieved and hashed; the public abstract supplies the headline replication results, while the underlying code and data are not retained here.
